name: Miro
tagline: Online collaborative whiteboard for diagrams, workshops, and planning

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Starter listed at $10/member/month monthly and $8/member/month annually.

verdictSummary: A simple multiplayer whiteboard is doable; Miro's value is scale, templates, integrations, facilitation, permissions, and reliability with many users.
coreLoopDIY: Build a canvas with sticky notes, shapes, connectors, comments, and optional multiplayer sync.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for workshops where dozens of people can join and everything still works.

priorArt.name: tldraw
priorArt.desc: Open-source canvas/whiteboard SDK and app; excellent prior art for DIY whiteboards.

notes: Good kinda because open-source makes the demo fast but production/workshop depth remains.
prompt:
Build me a personal replacement for Miro (Online collaborative whiteboard for diagrams, workshops, and planning). Requirements:

- Core loop: Build a canvas with sticky notes, shapes, connectors, comments, and optional multiplayer sync.
- Needs: canvas library.
- Needs: WebSocket/collab backend.
- Needs: database.
- Needs: auth.
- Needs: hosting.
- Needs: optional template library.
- Keep it personal-scale: no accounts, no telemetry, secrets in .env, SQLite or
  flat files for storage. Local-first wherever possible.
- Clean minimal UI where one is needed; CLI is fine where one is not.
- Include a README with setup steps, required keys, and any OS permissions.

Honest scope: this covers the core loop only. You will not get: large-board performance; templates; integrations.
